title: AI travel posters
subtitle: Pick one by what you already have
heading: AI travel poster prompts: pick one by what you already have
seoTitle: AI Travel Poster Prompts: City Collage, Perler Beads, Intaglio and Magazine | Image Prompt Book
lead: These travel posters start from different things. Some need only a place name. Some need your own photo or character. Some try to pack landmarks and information; others only need a mood. Look at what you have, then at what the picture has to do.

place-only.title: You only have a place name, and you want information

mood.title: Accuracy does not matter; you want a mood

own-assets.title: You already have a photo or a character

city-collage-postcard.why: A handwritten city name, landmark collage, map, postmark and coordinates go onto one 3:4 postcard. This is the densest information layout in the set.
city-collage-postcard.goodFor: A city souvenir card, or a festival card (add “端午” after the city name)
city-collage-postcard.notFor: Official print that needs exact coordinates or a correct map
city-collage-postcard.adjust: City: six options, or type your own

perler-bead-travel-editorial.why: The top half is a realistic sunset; the bottom half is a square perler-bead landmark and six bead badges. Photo and handmade each take half the page.
perler-bead-travel-editorial.goodFor: A series of pages that can reuse a country, a city or a theme
perler-bead-travel-editorial.notFor: A single illustration style with no realistic photo
perler-bead-travel-editorial.adjust: Place: five options, or replace with any location

surreal-futuristic-travel-poster.why: The city is invented: sculptural buildings, giant plants and floating pieces, in a low-saturation vintage travel-poster grain.
surreal-futuristic-travel-poster.goodFor: A concept poster, or an ideal city that does not map to a real place
surreal-futuristic-travel-poster.notFor: City publicity that has to show a real landmark

photo-illustration-travel-editorial.why: The same scene appears twice: a cinematic photograph and a spare illustration on ivory paper. There are two original prompts, Paris at sunset and a coastal lighthouse.
photo-illustration-travel-editorial.goodFor: A magazine-like vertical poster with little type
photo-illustration-travel-editorial.notFor: A layout that has to hold a lot of itinerary text
photo-illustration-travel-editorial.adjust: Sky or waves, caption and vertical ratio

photo-intaglio-study-poster.why: One area stays a real photograph; the same subject is redrawn next to it in banknote-like intaglio hatching, like a print study sheet.
photo-intaglio-study-poster.goodFor: Travel photos of buildings, bell towers or statues with a clear outline
photo-intaglio-study-poster.notFor: No reference photo, or a photo whose subject is small and broken up
photo-intaglio-study-poster.adjust: Format, comparison layout, paper-and-ink palette and sample text

tilted-character-travel-editorial.why: A close-up, steeply tilted character sits inside a tidy Japanese travel-magazine grid. The joke comes from that clash.
tilted-character-travel-editorial.goodFor: Travel publicity for an IP character, mascot or pet
tilted-character-travel-editorial.notFor: A serious city image or a landscape-only poster
tilted-character-travel-editorial.adjust: Entry side, expression and background; replace the character name in the prompt

choose: If you want a souvenir with a place name and landmarks quickly, try the city collage postcard first. For a quieter page that can become a series, switch to the perler-bead editorial.
If the picture does not have to match a real city, the surreal futuristic poster leaves room to invent, and the photo-and-illustration pair stays more like a magazine.
If you already have a photo, the intaglio study is the only one here that needs a reference image. If you have a character instead of a photo, use the tilted-character magazine poster.
caution: Place names, maps, coordinates and small type in every example are generated. Check them before you use the picture as official material.
